chunks: 3975 - Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

Regarding a man who sells an item, and the buyer says: it was for such-and-such, less than what the seller said, he said: "The statement is the statement of the seller if the item remains standing in its very form, along with his oath."

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man involved in the sale dispute
key_terms.الْبَائِعُ: the seller whose statement is accepted
key_terms.الْقَوْلُ: the legally accepted statement or claim
key_terms.قَائِمًا بِعَيْنِهِ: remaining in its original identifiable form
key_terms.يَبِيعُ: sells; enters into a sale transaction
key_terms.يَمِينِهِ: his oath, used to support the claim legally

ai.seo_question: In a dispute between a buyer and seller over the agreed price, whose word is accepted in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a dispute between a seller and a buyer over the sale price. It states that the seller's claim is accepted, with an oath, when the sold item is still present in its original condition. The report is significant in judicial rulings and commercial law, especially in resolving transactional disputes.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3975 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said

regarding a man who sells something and the buyer claims that it was sold for a lower price than what the seller stated:
"The statement of the seller is to be accepted if the item is still present in its original form, along with his oath."
